meta.title: Orchard — a garden weather station
meta.subtitle: Scoping
meta.headline: Let’s settle the sensor before we pour concrete.
meta.lede: Each decision below is pre-filled with a **recommended default** and the reasoning behind it. Review, override where you have a view, and flag anything to discuss.
meta.legend: Every question is pre-set to a recommended default (★). Change what you disagree with.
meta.closingAsk: Turn these into a build order and tell me what you still need from me.

constraints.label: Power:
constraints.text: mains socket in the shed, 12 m from the mast

constraints: No cloud account — the data stays on the home network

context.title: Site context
context.note: The station sits at the top of a ~0.4 ha orchard on a `north-facing` slope. Frost pockets form at the bottom, which is the whole reason for building it.

cards.title: Mast
cards.body: 3 m pole at the high corner, clear of the hedge.

cards.title: Shed
cards.body: Houses the receiver and the mains supply.

items.label: Read
items.desc: One sensor, one reading, written to disk.

items.label: Log
items.desc: Full sensor set on a schedule, with gaps handled.

items.label: Show
items.desc: A frost alert you actually trust at 5 a.m.
cold air pooling at the low end of the slope
the temperature at which the air gives up its moisture

blocks.heading: Note
blocks.text: Nothing here needs to survive a power cut for more than an hour.

questions.question: How does the mast talk to the shed?
questions.why: A 12 m trench for a cable is a weekend of digging; a 433 MHz link is an afternoon and the range is generous at this distance.

options.label: Buried cable
options.detail: Utterly reliable, but you are digging a trench.

options.label: Wi-Fi at the mast
options.detail: Needs power and coverage at the far corner.

questions.question: Which sensors go up first?
questions.why: Temperature and humidity give you the dew point, which is the one number a frost alert actually needs; wind is nice to have.

options.label: Temperature + humidity
options.detail: The minimum that answers the frost question.

options.label: The full set at once
options.detail: More to mount, more to debug, same first answer.

questions.question: Where do the readings live?
questions.why: A plain file per day is trivially inspectable and survives a machine rebuild; a database is a dependency you would be maintaining for one reader.

options.label: SQLite
options.detail: Queryable from day one; one more thing to back up.

options.label: One CSV per day
options.detail: Readable in anything, trivial to copy off.

options.label: Straight to a chart service
options.detail: Conflicts with keeping data off the cloud.

questions.question: How should a frost alert reach you?
questions.why: A push at 5 a.m. is the one that saves the blossom; the shed display is the one you glance at anyway.

options.label: Phone push
options.detail: Wakes you in time to light the candles.

options.label: Email
options.detail: You will read it at nine, which is too late.
